newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stock Exchange to begin Internet market.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stock Exchange to begin Internet market.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) said on Wednesday that it would establish an Internet-based market to help small to medium-sized unlisted companies raise capital for expansion.
The ASX said it would spend more than A$2 million on the project and had already set contracts for systems development.
ASX managing director Richard Humphry said the market would allow company owners to anonymously provide information about their company to potential investors.
"Internet technology is revolutionising the marketplace," Humphry said.
"It should be applied to this sector to help resolve the recurrent problem of capital shortages for small and medium businesses."
The ASX had liaised with the Australian Securities Commission on the development of the market, which would be coordinated by ASX official Barry Westlake.
